x: All three are correct: in 1546-47 Rama Raya backed Ahmadnagar against Bijapur and Bidar and took the Raichur doab, and in 1557-63 he backed Bijapur and razed Ahmadnagar - playing the Sultans against each other.

All four are correct: Venkatapati Raya II was called the 'Second Andhra Bhoja' (and 'Second Krishnadevaraya'), Appayya Dikshita (Shaivarka Mani Dipika) was at his court, his coins bore 'Om Venkateshwaraya Namah', and he defeated Veerappa Nayaka of Madurai at Vallankota.

D is the answer because Babur set up no administrative system at all (his rule had shallow roots and the treasury was empty), so 'a fully developed administrative system' was not one of his limitations. A, B and C are listed limits: the Afghans still claimed Delhi, Bengal stayed unconquered, and Gujarat-Malwa was united under Bahadur Shah.

Statements 1 and 2 are correct: Ibrahim Lodi was the last Delhi Sultan, and Panipat I was the first major field-artillery battle in North India. Statement 3 is false: Babur's authority had shallow roots and he left no administrative system, so Panipat did not create a consolidated Mughal administration.

The amin made the revenue assessment in Sher Shah's system. The shiqdar, qanungo and patwari were also revenue/local officials; none of them prepared manuscripts, commanded the cavalry or minted coins, so B, C and D are false pairs.

Hawkins reached Surat in 1608, in Jahangir's reign. B is wrong because Shah Abbas I captured Kandahar in 1622; its recovery in 1638 was under Shah Jahan, when Ali Mardan Khan surrendered it. C and D are wrong because Guru Arjan Dev backed the rebel Khusrau (not a rebellion against Khurram), and Mahabat Khan's coup was in 1626, not Khusrau's 1606 revolt.
All four are correct: Mumtaz Mahal was born Arjumand Banu Begum, was the daughter of Asaf Khan (Nur Jahan's brother), married Prince Khurram in 1612, and is entombed in the Taj Mahal.

The page's notes describe the Gaz-i-Ilahi (about 82 cm) used under Zabti as bamboo, so C. Other notes say the bamboo item was the jarib, made of bamboo pieces joined with iron rings in place of hemp rope; either way, the material was bamboo, not copper, stone or iron.
